test: wrela agent test, version 3: fresh agents change packages (make a shape, repair one, find a wrong pixel, stop a trap, make a GPU function cheaper), each graded by what was made and how it runs (grading.py), and each task run with and without the tools the superpowers plan added (run.py --tools). A new baseline, not comparable with version 2's.
brief:
You're changing a program in wrela, a new programming language for games, to measure how well agents use it. Read these files first, and only these (no other files in the repository: not the compiler, its tests or its standard library sources): {context}.

Your task ({id}): {task}

The package is {dir}/pkg: change its files there (it exists, with the files the task starts from). To compile, run exactly `{attempt} {dir}`, as a command of its own (not joined to another with `&&` or `;`): it builds the package, records the attempt and prints the compiler's diagnostics. You may also run these, each alone: {tools}. Those are the only commands allowed; don't run the compiler any other way. You have at most {max_attempts} attempts. Every attempt is graded by what the program makes and how it runs, by checks you can't see, so a program that builds but doesn't do what the task says counts as wrong: stop when it builds and you are confident it does what the task says.

When you're done, report: (1) whether it built, and on which attempt; (2) for each attempt, what you changed and why; (3) which commands helped, and anything in the language, its tools or its documentation that misled you.
